corrected_content.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral $$
\displaystyle \int_(C)\frac{y}{x}ds,
$$ where $C$ is the section of the curve $y = \frac{x^{2}}{2}$ between the points $(0, 0)$ and $(2, 2)$?
corrected_content.worked_solution:
Parametrize by $x=t$, $y=t^2/2$, $0\le t\le2$. Along the path, $y/x=t/2$ away from the origin and has limit $0$ there. Also $ds=\sqrt{1+t^2}\,dt$. Hence the integral, interpreted with this removable endpoint limit, is
$$\frac12\int_0^2t\sqrt{1+t^2}\,dt.$$
